questions.question: What are the mean and sample variance of [1,2,3,4]?
options: Mean 2.5 and variance 5/3
Mean 2.5 and variance 1.25
Mean 3 and variance 2
Mean 10 and variance 5
questions.explanation: The mean is 2.5. Squared deviations sum to 5, and sample variance divides by n-1=3, giving 5/3.

questions.question: Which statistic is least affected when one observation is an extreme outlier?
options: The mean
The median
The variance
The Pearson covariance
questions.explanation: The median depends on order and central position, so one extreme value usually does not move it much. Mean and spread statistics use the outlier's magnitude.

questions.question: When is Spearman correlation more appropriate than Pearson correlation?
options: When both variables are guaranteed independent
When every value must have the same rank
When the relationship is monotonic but not necessarily linear, or ranks are more reliable
When the goal is to prove that one variable causes the other
questions.explanation: Spearman computes Pearson correlation on ranks, so it detects monotonic association without requiring a straight-line relationship.

questions.question: What does a p-value of 0.03 mean in a test with a null hypothesis?
options: There is a 3% chance that the null hypothesis is true
The alternative hypothesis is 97% true
The observed effect is automatically important in practice
If the null were true, results at least this extreme would have probability about 0.03 under the test model
questions.explanation: A p-value is a tail probability conditional on the null and the test assumptions. It is not a posterior probability of either hypothesis or an effect-size measure.

questions.question: How does bootstrap_statistic form a confidence interval without assuming a normal population?
options: It repeatedly resamples the observed data with replacement and takes quantiles of the statistic
It replaces every observation with the population mean
It uses only the minimum and maximum of the original sample
It draws new labels from a uniform distribution
questions.explanation: The empirical sample acts as a proxy population. Repeated resamples approximate the sampling distribution of the chosen statistic, whose quantiles form the interval.

questions.question: A huge test set yields p<0.001 for a 0.1 percentage-point lift. What additional measure decides practical importance?
options: A smaller p-value from running the test again
Effect size and the business-relevant magnitude of the lift
The number of decimal places in the p-value
Whether the sample mean is exactly zero
questions.explanation: Large n can make tiny differences statistically detectable. Cohen's d or a domain-specific lift and cost threshold addresses whether the change matters.
